script: Basketball players who got CUT but refused to GIVE UP! Brandon Williams once walked into the Las Vegas Summer League with basically no NBA future, since he'd gone undrafted out of Arizona after a knee surgery wrecked his college career. In 2022, he led the Portland Trail Blazers all the way to the Summer League title, dropping 22 points in the championship game and hitting all ten of his free throws to bury the Knicks. But, a trophy from Vegas has a way of meaning nothing the moment the lights turn off. That October, Portland waived him, and Williams then started bouncing around the G League, where he put up huge numbers, over twenty points a game, and nobody in the NBA seemed to care as he spent time on four different teams while chasing one real shot. But over a year into that grind, an injury to someone else finally cracked the door open for him. The Mavericks signed him to a two-way deal, and at first he was just a name at the end of the bench until their backcourt got wiped out by injuries. Suddenly Williams was thrown into real minutes and he went off, averaging around 15 points and four assists over his final fifteen games while even scoring a career high 31 points against Memphis. Dallas rewarded him with a standard contract, and the guy everyone gave up on played 66 games the next season and became a real NBA rotation player. So the Summer League legend who looked like he'd never make it... actually made it.
